case.pattern_description: A coordinated card-not-present campaign across multiple cardholders where attackers systematically generate new device profiles behind anonymous proxies to make unauthorized high-value product-C purchases between $510 and $963. The perpetrators deliberately rotate hardware identifiers between transactions to avoid detection by device-fingerprinting and graph-clustering algorithms. This syndicated cross-account attack fits none of the standard static patterns due to intentional device dissociation.

evidence.claim: Flagged transaction 3660127 received a low model score of 0.008 with a historical fraud rate of 0.0063 and legacy risk score of 0.07.
Transaction 3660127 was conducted using device D009721, which was marked as New for the account and operated behind an anonymous proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS).

Flagged transaction 3660127 is the third transaction in a run of three high-value online product-C transactions totaling $2,166.71 between 2017-01-17 and 2017-01-19 (3660125 for $637.13, 3660126 for $758.80, and 3660127 for $770.78), all using new devices behind anonymous proxies on a card with no prior online product-C baseline.

Three other cards belonging to different customers (C05061-K1, C10553-K1, and C07925-K1) exhibited the exact same signature of 2+ online product-C purchases between $510 and $963 from new devices behind anonymous proxies between 2017-01-12 and 2017-01-17, identifying an active cross-customer syndicate.

evidence.claim: The holder baseline has only 1 prior transaction of $97.95 for product R, with flagged transaction 3660127 being new for product C, using a new device, and exceeding the prior maximum amount ($770.78 vs $97.95) with no recurring pattern.

Card C06220-K1 has 6 prior closed cases including 5 confirmed fraud outcomes (CC-5379, CC-4224, CC-2807, CC-2539, CC-0626) involving online card-not-present and out-of-region card-present fraud, and only 1 cleared alert (CC-0815).

Device D009721 and region 126 in the 7-day window around transaction 3660127 show zero transactions with model scores over 0.5 and lift of 0.0 versus baseline, reflecting deliberate device and region rotation to evade single-element link analysis.

case.summary: Investigation of alert HHF-002 on card C06220-K1 identified an undocumented, syndicated card-not-present fraud scheme. Between January 17 and January 19, 2017, the card was subjected to three unauthorized online product-C charges totaling $2,166.71 (transactions 3660125, 3660126, and 3660127). Each transaction utilized a different newly introduced device (D009715, D009718, and D009721) operating behind anonymous proxies, matching identical attack patterns seen on peer cards C05061-K1, C07925-K1, and C10553-K1. The activity was confirmed as fraud with a probability of 0.93, resulting in card blocking, case escalation, regulatory reporting under Policy R9, and monitoring of connected accounts.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details a coordinated card-not-present fraud scheme targeting customer C06220 on card C06220-K1, alongside related unauthorized transactions identified across peer cards C05061-K1, C07925-K1, and C10553-K1. Between January 17, 2017, and January 19, 2017, card C06220-K1 incurred three unauthorized online purchases for product C totaling $2,166.71. The sequential charges comprised transaction 3660125 for $637.13 on January 17 in region 330, transaction 3660126 for $758.80 on January 18 in region 384, and transaction 3660127 for $770.78 on January 19 in region 126. Each unauthorized transaction was conducted through a new device identifier—D009715, D009718, and D009721 respectively—and routed through anonymous internet proxy connections (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS). The perpetrator also varied the associated contact emails across domains including anonymous.com, comcast.net, and verizon.net. This activity marked a complete departure from the cardholder's historical baseline, which contained zero product-C transactions across the prior 60 days. Scheme analysis revealed that three cards belonging to distinct customers—C05061-K1, C07925-K1, and C10553-K1—experienced the identical pattern of repeated online product-C charges between $510 and $963 from new devices behind anonymous proxies between January 12, 2017, and January 17, 2017. The deliberate rotation of device identifiers and IP proxies across multiple customer accounts demonstrates an organized syndicated effort to evade automated fraud filters and single-device link detection. Card C06220-K1 has been blocked, connected accounts have been placed under monitoring, and this filing is submitted under Policy R9 for undocumented coordinated fraud.

stop_reason: The investigation stopped pursuant to Policy Section 6 because the fraud probability reached a decisive level of 0.93 (exceeding the 0.85 threshold) supported by multiple independent evidence bases, including coordinated cross-card patterns, anomalous device and proxy usage, and abrupt departure from cardholder baseline. Additional verification steps would not alter the determination of coordinated syndicated fraud.
